title: unified-rollouts-enhance-shadow-canary-ab-autorollback-stability-guards
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: We continue to see flakiness in staged shadow/canary A/B rollouts where transient signal noise or low sample counts cause premature automatic rollbacks. This PR adds stability guards and signal validation to the unified rollouts autorollback engine to reduce false-positive rollbacks while preserving fast reaction to real regressions.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds "min_sample_window" and "min_signal_samples" guardrails to metric-driven autorollback so threshold checks require a minimum number of samples before triggering.
- Introduces composite-metric smoothing using a rolling-histogram + median aggregation to reduce sensitivity to single-signal spikes.
- Adds a small, configurable cooldown window after a rollback action to prevent repeated flip-flop rollbacks during noisy periods.
- Fixes a race condition in the rollback worker that could cause duplicate rollback events under high concurrency.
- Enhances observability: new metrics (rollout.autorollback.evaluations_total, rollout.autorollback.false_positives, rollout.autorollback.cooldown_active) and additional tracing spans for the evaluation path.
- Adds end-to-end integration tests that simulate shadow + canary traffic patterns and assert no rollback for transient spikes and correct rollback on sustained degradation.
- Updates rollout docs with recommended defaults and knobs for SRE teams.

Implementation notes:
- Core guard logic is in rollout/autorollback/engine.go. The engine now requires both a metric threshold breach and a min_sample_window satisfied before incrementing a failure counter.
- Composite metric evaluation lives in rollout/autorollback/metrics_eval.go and exposes a smoothing mode (median, mean, percentile) selectable per-rollout. Defaults to median.
- A short-lived mutex + idempotency token was added to the rollback worker (controller/rollback_worker.go) to avoid concurrent rollbacks for the same rollout id.
- Tests: e2e/rollouts/stability_test.py contains traffic generators and assertions; unit tests added under rollout/autorollback/*_test.go. CI config updated to run the integration test in the rollouts matrix.

Checklist:
- [x] Add stability guards and config knobs
- [x] Observable metrics and traces
- [x] Unit + e2e tests
- [x] Docs update and recommended defaults
- [x] Fix concurrency/race in rollback worker

Related: ENG-1189 (stability guards), ENG-1190 (rollback worker fixes), SUP-4231 (customer reported flapping during canary rollout).

Notes for reviewers: The default values are conservative and intended to reduce noise-driven rollbacks for hosted customers; Dedicated/private customers can tune via rollout policy. We should monitor rollout.autorollback.false_positives for 2 weeks post-merge before tightening thresholds further.

review_comments: Raj Patel: Overall looks good. Can you add an explicit end-to-end case for a burst spike followed by normal traffic? Concerned about perf impact of rolling-histogram for very high QPS.
Ava Martinez: Added e2e burst test and added sampling fallback for QPS > 5k; histogram uses reservoir sampling in high QPS mode (see metrics_eval.go).
Elena Gomez: Please add telemetry for cooldown_active and track cooldowns per-rollout id. Also flagging potential N+1 DB call in controller — please address.
Ava Martinez: Added cooldown_active metric and converted controller query to batched fetch. Addressed N+1 with a rollout id batch resolver.
Samir O'Neill: Verified the race fix locally and in stress runs. Approving after CI completes.
release_notes: Stability guards for autorollback: reduce false-positive rollouts by requiring minimum sample windows and adding cooldowns; new metrics and e2e tests. No breaking changes; rollout behavior can be tuned via rollout policy config.
post_merge_actions: Monitor rollout.autorollback.false_positives (SLO: decrease by 50% vs baseline)
Add config toggle to Dedicated defaults if customers need earlier behavior
Backport hotfix to release/2025-11 if we detect regressions in the next 48h
